Is there a movement to get rid of Pao and the current SJW mindset on reddit here?

I don't think that orchestrating such an operation would really be beneficial. We might as well just carry on here how we want to. Reddit is a business, they've made a decision. It's their site, they can make whatever decisions they want. The changes at reddit were not made rashly or without thought. They knew which of their users would welcome them and which of their users would be unhappy with them. They made a business choice regarding which demographic to cater to.

We didn't "lose" a fight. There was no fight. Our input, opinions, etc don't factor into their decision in the least.

Look at this way, there's a coffee shop that all the hipsters hang out at, talking about all of their hipster things, and showing each other pictures of their cats, and whatnot - the coffee shop is hip as fuck and serves lattes made with either milk or soy. One day, the hip coffee shop decides that they are only going to serve soy lattes because that's what people should be drinking. A few of the hardcore soy hipsters are excited and think that the overall quality of the coffee shop will improve because it now caters to them more specifically. Everyone else feels like they've been told to drink soy and shut up so they go to a different coffee shop that serves soy and milk lattes and hang out there. It's the same people doing the same things just doing them at a different location. After awhile the new coffee shop becomes the hip place because all of the hipsters are there, also because the old coffee shop will kick you out if you talk about milk.

I agree. There was no fight lost, because there was never a fight, and, most importantly, because there is no reason for a fight. They're a commercial business, trying to become more mainstream because that is what brings in advertisers. The target audience of this policy i not the current users, who might be upset and leave, but the much more numerous potential users that are the current userbase of Facebook.

There is one point, however, where I do disagree: I don't think they thought this through very well. Not specifically this action, but their whole strategy. The life-cycle of sites like theirs seems to be: start as a rather niche forum, become more popular, realise increased popularity means increased revenue, try to become even more popular, become generic and bland, decline and fall into limbo. Many websites can be seen in different stages of this cycle, LiveJournal, MySpace, Slashdot, digg, and also reddit.

The only sites, in my opinion, that have a chance to not follow this path are those that are maintained purely not for profit, as there will be, for those sites, no incentive to increase popularity, or at least not at the cost of the original community, since there is no increase in revenue comming with it.

More power to you if you want to fight it out. I however believe that the fight is not worth it. Those who support the new SJW direction are dug in like ticks, some with the support of the Admins (SRS). I think it's best to plan for the eventual downfall of reddit just as with dig. To prepare we should start all of the popular subs on reddit and any chance we get on voat we should challenge them and let them know that we will not conform to their beliefs. The big thing is to get a foothold in the larger subs and to screen the mods to avoid giving them influence on the more popular subs.

Anyway that's just my opinion.
